painTitle: The outbound gap in your service stack

pain.heading: Clients keep asking, you keep stalling
pain.body: Every quarter another client asks for lead-gen or outbound. Building that delivery capability in-house is slow, expensive, and pulls focus from what you already do well.

pain.heading: Bad outsourcing burns your name
pain.body: Handing outbound off to an unreliable freelancer or overseas shop means sloppy emails and spam complaints land under your agency's reputation, not theirs.

pain.heading: The whole account walks

caseCards.headline: A new $8K/month revenue line, with zero delivery hires
caseCards.body: A 10-person performance marketing agency kept getting asked for lead-gen and outbound by existing retainer clients but had no bandwidth to build it. They became a Myntmore partner, we ran cold email and LinkedIn outreach for two of their clients under the agency's own branding, and the agency simply added it as a new managed service line, billed and reported entirely under their name.

caseCards.headline: Kept a $60K/year retainer that was about to walk
caseCards.body: A fractional CMO consultant had a client asking for outbound pipeline generation as part of the engagement, something outside her own skill set. Rather than lose the account to a full-service agency, she brought Myntmore in as her white-label delivery partner. The client only ever interacted with her; Myntmore ran ICP mapping, list building, and outreach behind the scenes.

caseCards.headline: Turned a one-off referral habit into recurring commission
caseCards.body: A branding studio used to informally refer outbound work to freelancers and never saw a rupee for it. As a Myntmore partner, every referral now runs through a tracked partner agreement: the studio scopes the client, Myntmore executes cold email and ABM under the studio's brand, and the studio earns a recurring margin for as long as the client stays active.
